findings.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — The LRU cache key is only key+locale+backend id and ignores the fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale), so in multisite a fallback string resolved for site A (default :fr) is served to site B (default :de) for the same user locale, and stays stale after an admin changes default_locale.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:9 — Fallbacks are now included in every environment (test/dev included, not just production), and :en is always the last fallback, so a key missing in a non-English locale silently returns English instead of "translation missing", and literal `default:` values are skipped whenever an :en translation exists.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — Fallback locale files are only eager-loaded in ApplicationController#set_locale; jobs, mailers, rake tasks and rescue_from error pages that run before or without this filter look up fallback locales that were never loaded, and translate caches the resulting "translation missing" text in the LRU with no invalidation when those locales load later.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — Fallbacks#translate calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on every uncached translation, so every I18n.t (including uncached calls with interpolation args, and error-page rendering) now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale; if SiteSetting errors or returns nil (boot, migrations, precompile without DB), nil.to_sym raises and every translation fails site-wide.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:12 — FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides only [], so callers expecting the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks API (defaults, defaults=, map, fetch, key?) get an empty hash or NoMethodError; if anything reassigns I18n.fallbacks to a standard object, the ensure_loaded! call in set_locale raises NoMethodError on every request.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:63 — ensure_loaded! lazily initializes and reads the process-global @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, while translate (line 68) still assumes it is non-nil, so correctness depends on the call order and on the GIL.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — Translate LRU cache key is key+locale+backend only, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so fallback-resolved strings leak across multisite sites and stay stale after the site default locale changes.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — Fallback locales are eager-loaded only in ApplicationController#set_locale while translate loads just config.locale, so in jobs/mailers/rake/specs fallbacks silently miss and the "translation missing" result is cached and never invalidated once fallback locales load.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — set_locale hard-depends on the custom FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, so if any env/gem still sets config.i18n.fallbacks the Rails i18n railtie (after_initialize, after this initializer) replaces I18n.fallbacks with I18n::Locale::Fallbacks and every request raises NoMethodError.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — .compact` cannot guard a nil/blank SiteSetting.default_locale because `.to_sym` runs first (nil raises NoMethodError, "" yields :"" which is then loaded and looked up as a locale).

config/initializers/i18n.rb:12 — FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash and overrides only `[]`, so callers using the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks API (defaults, defaults=, compute) or Hash access like fetch/values_at get errors or empty results instead of the fallback chain.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — The process-wide LRU cache key (key + config.locale + backend.object_id) doesn't include SiteSetting.default_locale or the current site, so strings resolved through fallback get cached and served stale after default_locale changes, or to other multisite tenants with a different default locale.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — FallbackLocaleList#[] is not memoized, so every backend translate call (including all I18n.t calls with interpolation/count/default args, which always skip the accelerator cache) allocates 3 arrays and does a SiteSetting.default_locale lookup plus to_sym, roughly 1-3us per call on the hottest i18n path.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:69 — Args-bearing I18n.t calls are never cached, so a missing key now walks up to 3 locales on every call, and each miss throws and allocates a MissingTranslation, where before there was a single lookup.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — ensure_loaded! eagerly loads the default_locale and :en YAML files in every worker, even when no fallback is ever needed, which adds resident memory per process and first-request latency for each locale while holding the global LOAD_MUTEX.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — translate only lazy-loads config.locale and ensure_loaded! is wired only into ApplicationController#set_locale, so Sidekiq jobs/mailers/console never load the site-default or :en fallback locales and emit "translation missing" strings nondeterministically depending on which locales the process happened to load.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — LRU cache key is key+locale+backend id and omits the fallback chain, so in multisite (per-site default_locale) or after an admin changes default_locale, a fallback-resolved string (or a cached "translation missing" string from a non-request context) is served process-wide to other sites/requests until eviction.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — Unguarded call to the custom FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! raises NoMethodError on every request if I18n.fallbacks is replaced by a stock I18n::Locale::Fallbacks (e.g. any env/operator/plugin config still setting config.i18n.fallbacks, which the Rails i18n railtie applies in after_initialize, after this initializer).

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — With Fallbacks included, every uncached I18n.t now calls SiteSetting.default_locale, making translation depend on SiteSetting/DB availability during boot, rake tasks, migrations and asset precompile where it previously had no DB dependency.
config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — .compact is ineffective because nil.to_sym raises NoMethodError before compaction, so a nil/unset default_locale breaks every translation instead of being skipped.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:63 — @loaded_locales ||= [] and the include? check run outside LOAD_MUTEX, so concurrent threads (or a concurrent reload!) can race on initializing/replacing the array in multi-threaded servers.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — The new global fallback chain (user locale -> site default -> :en) changes behavior but ships with no specs for order, including a key present only in the site default locale.

config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — No coverage for dedupe or edge inputs (user locale == default, default == :en, nil locale, nil/blank SiteSetting.default_locale where `.to_sym` runs before `.compact`).

config/initializers/i18n.rb:9 — Fallbacks are now included globally, including the test env (previously only production/profile), so specs that looked up keys missing in non-en locales now silently pass with the English text instead of failing.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — No test covers the interaction with the LRU cache, whose key ignores SiteSetting.default_locale, so a cached fallback result goes stale when the default locale changes.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — No test covers translation outside a request (jobs/mailers/rake) where only config.locale is loaded, so fallback locales are never loaded and "translation missing" gets cached.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:62 — No spec checks that the new I18n.ensure_loaded! is idempotent (no reload of an already-loaded locale), that it works before @loaded_locales is initialized, or that it behaves correctly after reload! resets state.
config/initializers/i18n.rb:20 — No spec checks that FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! loads every locale in the chain for the current I18n.locale.

app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — No controller/request spec checks that set_locale loads fallback locales before rendering (e.g. a user with a fr locale on a de-default site sees de/en text for keys missing in fr).

config/initializers/i18n.rb:5 — Pluralization setup moved out of the deleted pluralization.rb into i18n.rb (now loaded after the freedom patches) with no regression spec for pluralized lookups through the fallback path (count args bypass the cache via translate_no_cache).

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — The LRU cache key is only key+locale+backend id and ignores the fallback chain (SiteSetting.default_locale), so in multisite a fallback string resolved for site A (default :fr) is served to site B (default :de) for the same user locale, and stays stale after an admin changes default_locale.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any LRU cache key construction or logic that combines `key+locale+backend id`, nor any multisite scoping in the cache. The only relevant changes are adding `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `set_locale`, defining a custom `FallbackLocaleList` that references `SiteSetting.default_locale`, and adding `ensure_loaded!(locale)` to `TranslateAccelerator`. Without the cache-key code in the diff, the claim about serving fallback strings across sites / staleness after `default_locale` changes is not verifiable from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:9 — Fallbacks are now included in every environment (test/dev included, not just production), and :en is always the last fallback, so a key missing in a non-English locale silently returns English instead of "translation missing", and literal `default:` values are skipped whenever an :en translation exists.

adjudication.rationale: The new initializer `config/initializers/i18n.rb` unconditionally includes `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, which will run in all environments (including dev/test). `FallbackLocaleList#[]` always returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`, making `:en` a guaranteed final fallback. With fallbacks enabled, missing keys in a non-English locale can resolve to an English translation (and `default:` options would not be used if a fallback translation exists). This is a real behavioral change, but it appears intentional per the inline comment (“user locale, site locale, english”), so it’s more of a scope/behavior concern than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — Fallback locale files are only eager-loaded in ApplicationController#set_locale; jobs, mailers, rake tasks and rescue_from error pages that run before or without this filter look up fallback locales that were never loaded, and translate caches the resulting "translation missing" text in the LRU with no invalidation when those locales load later.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds fallback-locale eager loading only in `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb). The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` explicitly loads `I18n.locale`, `SiteSetting.default_locale`, and `:en` by calling `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, but there are no other call sites added in the diff for non-controller contexts (jobs/mailers/rake/tasks). Meanwhile `TranslateAccelerator#translate` still only auto-loads `config.locale` (not fallback locales), so any I18n fallback lookup outside the controller filter can occur before fallback locales are loaded, yielding missing translations and (given the accelerator’s caching behavior) plausibly caching the miss until restart. This is a correctness issue exposed by moving away from `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` to a manual load trigger in the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — Fallbacks#translate calls I18n.fallbacks[locale] on every uncached translation, so every I18n.t (including uncached calls with interpolation args, and error-page rendering) now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale; if SiteSetting errors or returns nil (boot, migrations, precompile without DB), nil.to_sym raises and every translation fails site-wide.

adjudication.rationale: The new initializer defines `FallbackLocaleList#[]` to return `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]...`. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is `nil` (or `SiteSetting` cannot be queried during boot/migrations/assets precompile without DB), `nil.to_sym` will raise, breaking translation resolution. This code path is exercised via the I18n fallbacks backend (it consults `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`) and is also now invoked explicitly in `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which calls `self[I18n.locale]` and thus hits `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on each request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:12 — FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides only [], so callers expecting the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks API (defaults, defaults=, map, fetch, key?) get an empty hash or NoMethodError; if anything reassigns I18n.fallbacks to a standard object, the ensure_loaded! call in set_locale raises NoMethodError on every request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a custom `I18n.fallbacks` object (`FallbackLocaleList < Hash`) that only customizes `[]` and adds a nonstandard `ensure_loaded!`, and `ApplicationController#set_locale` now unconditionally calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. From the diff alone, it’s not provably broken because the initializer sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, so `ensure_loaded!` exists. However, the finding’s concern is grounded: this object does not implement the broader `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` API (e.g., `defaults`), so other code expecting that API could fail, and the controller now assumes `I18n.fallbacks` always responds to `ensure_loaded!` (making later reassignment/overrides risky).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:63 — ensure_loaded! lazily initializes and reads the process-global @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, while translate (line 68) still assumes it is non-nil, so correctness depends on the call order and on the GIL.

lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — Translate LRU cache key is key+locale+backend only, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so fallback-resolved strings leak across multisite sites and stay stale after the site default locale changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes fallback behavior to depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale` at runtime (`FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`). That means the resolved translation for a given `I18n.locale` can change when the site default locale differs (e.g., multisite) or is updated. `TranslateAccelerator` continues to treat the active locale as the primary dimension it loads/caches against (e.g., `translate` ensures `config.locale` is loaded; added `ensure_loaded!` only tracks `@loaded_locales` by locale). If its LRU cache keying does not incorporate the site default locale/fallback chain (as the finding claims), cached fallback results could be reused incorrectly across different `default_locale` values, leading to stale/wrong strings after changing the site default locale or between sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — Fallback locales are eager-loaded only in ApplicationController#set_locale while translate loads just config.locale, so in jobs/mailers/rake/specs fallbacks silently miss and the "translation missing" result is cached and never invalidated once fallback locales load.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `ApplicationController#set_locale` now calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, and `TranslateAccelerator#translate` still loads only `config.locale`. However, the finding’s core claim—that fallbacks “silently miss” outside controllers and that a “translation missing” is cached forever until fallback locales load—cannot be verified from the diff. Rails’ fallback backend typically retries lookups per-fallback locale (which would cause `config.locale` to change and `load_locale` to run for each), and the diff does not show the caching behavior or any demonstrated lack of cache invalidation for missing keys. The jobs/mailers/rake/spec behavior is also not evidenced in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — set_locale hard-depends on the custom FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, so if any env/gem still sets config.i18n.fallbacks the Rails i18n railtie (after_initialize, after this initializer) replaces I18n.fallbacks with I18n::Locale::Fallbacks and every request raises NoMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `ApplicationController#set_locale` call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (new line in `app/controllers/application_controller.rb`). That method exists only on the newly introduced `FallbackLocaleList` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, where `I18n.fallbacks` is set to an instance of that class. If `I18n.fallbacks` is later replaced with a different fallbacks implementation that doesn’t define `ensure_loaded!`, this will raise `NoMethodError` at request time. The specific claim about Rails railtie overriding `I18n.fallbacks` when `config.i18n.fallbacks` is set is not directly verifiable from the diff, but the hard dependency on the custom `ensure_loaded!` is grounded in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — .compact` cannot guard a nil/blank SiteSetting.default_locale because `.to_sym` runs first (nil raises NoMethodError, "" yields :"" which is then loaded and looked up as a locale).

adjudication.rationale: In `FallbackLocaleList#[]`, the array is built as `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`, so `.compact` cannot prevent `nil.to_sym` (would raise) and will not remove an empty-string default locale once it becomes `:""`. The diff doesn’t show whether `SiteSetting.default_locale` can ever be `nil`/blank, so this is a real edge-case robustness issue but not conclusively a currently-triggerable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:12 — FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash and overrides only `[]`, so callers using the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks API (defaults, defaults=, compute) or Hash access like fetch/values_at get errors or empty results instead of the fallback chain.

adjudication.rationale: The diff sets `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new`, where `FallbackLocaleList` is a `Hash` subclass that only customizes `[]` (and adds `ensure_loaded!`). If any code (Rails/I18n internals or app code) expects `I18n.fallbacks` to behave like `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` (e.g., `defaults`, `compute`, etc.) rather than just supporting `[]`, this change could cause `NoMethodError`/unexpected behavior. The diff itself only shows `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` usage, so the breakage is a compatibility risk rather than a directly verifiable defect from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 — The process-wide LRU cache key (key + config.locale + backend.object_id) doesn't include SiteSetting.default_locale or the current site, so strings resolved through fallback get cached and served stale after default_locale changes, or to other multisite tenants with a different default locale.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a custom `I18n.fallbacks` (using `SiteSetting.default_locale`) and an `ensure_loaded!` helper, but it does not show the translate accelerator’s LRU cache key construction or any process-wide cache behavior. The finding’s specific claim about a cache key of `(key + config.locale + backend.object_id)` omitting `SiteSetting.default_locale`/multisite context cannot be verified from the provided diff hunks, and the cited line number doesn’t correspond to any cache-key logic in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — FallbackLocaleList#[] is not memoized, so every backend translate call (including all I18n.t calls with interpolation/count/default args, which always skip the accelerator cache) allocates 3 arrays and does a SiteSetting.default_locale lookup plus to_sym, roughly 1-3us per call on the hottest i18n path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `FallbackLocaleList#[]` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` that returns a freshly allocated array each time and performs `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every call (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded potential performance concern if `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` is invoked frequently. However, the finding’s broader claim about it impacting “every backend translate call” and microsecond-level costs cannot be verified from the diff alone, so it’s not a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:69 — Args-bearing I18n.t calls are never cached, so a missing key now walks up to 3 locales on every call, and each miss throws and allocates a MissingTranslation, where before there was a single lookup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `TranslateAccelerator#translate` bypasses caching whenever `args.length > 0` (`return translate_no_cache(key, *args)`), so any repeated args-bearing lookups won’t benefit from the accelerator’s cache. Separately, the new initializer configures fallbacks to try up to three locales (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`), so a missing translation can now trigger multiple backend lookups per call. However, the claim about "each miss throws and allocates a MissingTranslation" and that "before there was a single lookup" is not directly verifiable from the shown code (previous fallback chain length/behavior isn’t fully shown, and exception/allocation behavior depends on I18n internals/options). Overall this is a concrete, diff-grounded performance concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/application_controller.rb:159 — ensure_loaded! eagerly loads the default_locale and :en YAML files in every worker, even when no fallback is ever needed, which adds resident memory per process and first-request latency for each locale while holding the global LOAD_MUTEX.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` to `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so it will run per request. The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` explicitly iterates `self[I18n.locale]` which returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` and calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each, meaning default locale and `:en` get loaded in each worker on first use even if no fallback lookup occurs. This is a concrete perf/memory/latency concern created by the change (though not a correctness bug). The part about holding a global `LOAD_MUTEX` is plausible but not directly shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — translate only lazy-loads config.locale and ensure_loaded! is wired only into ApplicationController#set_locale, so Sidekiq jobs/mailers/console never load the site-default or :en fallback locales and emit "translation missing" strings nondeterministically depending on which locales the process happened to load.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unguarded `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, and `ensure_loaded!` is only defined on the newly introduced `FallbackLocaleList` (a custom `Hash`) in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. adjudication_records.issue_text: config/initializers/i18n.rb:17 — The new global fallback chain (user locale -> site default -> :en) changes behavior but ships with no specs for order, including a key present only in the site default locale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68 — No test covers translation outside a request (jobs/mailers/rake) where only config.locale is loaded, so fallback locales are never loaded and "translation missing" gets cached.
